title: Beats 360 Over-Ear Headphones Leak in Retail Listings
author: Juli Clover
content:
One of the Beats codenames MacRumors found in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 update (B518) appears to be for the Beats 360, a new set of over-ear headphones that we could see launch soon.
![Beats 360 Feature](https://images.macrumors.com/t/NuuGj437VjDZGYrqQk2Z21QllXs=/400x0/article-new/2026/08/Beats-360-Feature.jpg?lossy)
Multiple Reddit users found signs of the Beats 360 on UK websites like Amazon, though those listings have now been removed.
The headphones have a look that is distinct from the existing Beats Studio Pro over-ear headphones, featuring a rounder design with AirPods Max-like mesh fabric ear cups and headband. The ear cups and headband will be replaceable with interchangeable cushion options. The headphones will ship with Performance Knit cushions, but an UltraPlush option will also be available. Beats will sell the headphones in Pink, Black, Sky, and Cloud. Volt and Navy may also be color options, but there are only listings for cushions in the shades.
One listing says these are the first-ever sweat-resistant and water-resistant over-ear headphones Beats has come out with, so it sounds like they should be better for wearing during workouts than current Beats over-ear options. From the listing:
- Beats 360 have interchangeable cushion options for both ear cups and headband, so you can have a fresh set ready after your workout or a new colour just to switch up your look. These over-ear noise-cancelling headphones are built for active lifestyles and all-day comfort.
- Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) blocks out unwanted noise to help you focus, after adapting to your environment and unique fit - with up to 1.75x more noise cancellation than Beats Studio Pro.
- The bespoke, high-fidelity acoustic platform delivers powerful bass and pinpoint precision across the tonal range with ultra-low distortion for the ultimate listening experience. Personalised spatial audio with dynamic head tracking delivers immersive surround sound.
- Ear cushions are built from acoustically engineered memory foam and shaped to fit comfortably over your ears, forming an optimal seal for incredible sound.
- Exceptional call quality powered by an advanced Al-trained algorithm and beam-forming mic system that filters out background noise.
- Our first-ever sweat- and water-resistant over-ear headphones, with an IPX4 rating to ensure they're built to go everywhere you do.
- All-day battery life for extended playback even with ANC on.
- Compatible with both Apple and Android for one-touch pairing and more. Easy-to-use controls are positioned on the back of each ear cup, including a volume rocker, a multifunction button to control music and calls, a power button and a listening mode button.
- Fold-flat design for extra comfort and convenience. Woven ripstop fabric case included.
- What's in the box: Beats 360 true wireless over-ear headphones with interchangeable performance knit cushions, woven ripstop fabric carrying case, warranty card and Quick Start Guide. Additional Beats 360 cushion kits, USB-C charging cable and power adapter sold separately.
Pricing is expected to start at $299 in the United States. There's no word on when the new Beats headphones will launch, but with listings popping up, they could come anytime.
We previously saw signs of the new headphones in May, when the U.S. Federal Communications Commission published documents featuring the rounded design that's showing up on product pages, and in July when Beats gave them to World Cup players as a teaser.
summary: Retail listings and code references indicate that Beats is preparing to launch the Beats 360 over-ear headphones, featuring a round design with interchangeable mesh cushions. Priced around $299, they will be the brand's first sweat- and water-resistant over-ear headphones, boasting improved Active Noise Cancelling and all-day battery life. The headphones have previously been teased by the FCC and given to World Cup players.
key_points: The Beats 360 are over-ear headphones featuring a rounder design with AirPods Max-like mesh fabric and replaceable ear cup and headband cushions.
They are Beats' first-ever sweat- and water-resistant over-ear headphones with an IPX4 rating.
Key features include Active Noise Cancelling with up to 1.75x more cancellation than Beats Studio Pro, personalized spatial audio, and all-day battery life.
Pricing is expected to start at $299 in the United States, with color options including Pink, Black, Sky, and Cloud.
They offer Apple and Android compatibility, physical controls on the back of each ear cup, and a fold-flat design with a woven ripstop fabric case.

title: New Xperia 10 VIII reveals itself in leak as Sony confirms global launch
author: Alex Alderson
content:
Sony has finally confirmed details about its next 'Xperia New Product Announcement'. For the time being, the company is remaining quiet about what exactly it has in store. However, a new Geekbench listing indicates that the new Xperia is already with reviewers.
Last month, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) revealed that Sony had developed a new smartphone to complement the Xperia 1 VIII that we reviewed earlier this year. Although the US regulatory body only shared charging information and a handful of details about the device, a previous leak suggested that the Xperia 10 VIII would launch with XQ-GH44, XQ-GH54 and XQ-GH74 model numbers.
Now, the middle of those three has appeared on Geekbench. Surprisingly, the listing reports that Sony has equipped the XQ-GH54 with the same chipset as the Xperia 10 VII (curr. $549 on Amazon). While the benchmarking platform does show the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 outright, the 'QTI SM6475' name matches Qualcomm's part number for the chipset inside the Xperia 10 VII.
Additionally, Geekbench reports that Sony has equipped the Xperia 10 VIII with 8 GB of RAM. Sony will officially launch its new Xperia 10 on August 25 at 02:00 UTC. Pricing, availability and other hardware specifications remain unknown for now, as does whether the Xperia 10 VIII will carry over its predecessor's design.
![](https://www.notebookcheck.net/fileadmin/_processed_/2/0/csm_xperia-10-viii-confirmed-and-geekbench-bottom_968a8b5bad.jpg)
summary: Sony has confirmed an upcoming Xperia new product launch event for August 25. Ahead of the announcement, a Geekbench listing for the new Xperia 10 VIII model revealed it features 8 GB of RAM and the same Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 chipset as its predecessor. Additional details regarding pricing, full specifications, and design remain unannounced.
key_points: Sony scheduled its new Xperia product launch for August 25.
A Geekbench listing for model XQ-GH54 indicates the device is the Xperia 10 VIII.
The new smartphone is equipped with 8 GB of RAM.
The device retains the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 chipset used in the Xperia 10 VII.

title: LG’s new OLED breakthrough can boost display lifespans
author: Jess Weatherbed
content:
LG Display has unveiled a new OLED manufacturing method that reportedly results in panels that are brighter, longer-lasting, more efficient, and theoretically can be almost any size. This new technology is called FLiPP (FMM-Less innovative Pixel Patterning), which LG Display describes as a “dream next-generation OLED” patterning method that aims to eliminate some of the existing limitations in OLED panels.
LG’s new OLED breakthrough can boost display lifespans
The ‘FLiPP’ tech should also be brighter, more energy efficient, and virtually any size.
![LG Display FLiPP OLED hero](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/LG-Display-FLiPP-OLED-hero.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
![LG Display FLiPP OLED hero](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/LG-Display-FLiPP-OLED-hero.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
The main advantage of FLiPP is that it doesn’t use a fine metal mask (FMM) like conventional RGB OLEDs, which is a metal plate with tiny holes used to stencil light-emitting materials for pixel patterning. This manufacturing process can be costly, and larger panels can suffer from sagging and alignment problems. Instead, FLiPP positions RGB pixels in order and then uses photolithography and UV light to remove areas that aren’t needed.
Compared to FMM panels, LG Display says that FLiPP enables OLED panels to be 1.6 times brighter and last 2.4 times longer, and reduces power consumption by 13 percent. FLiPP is also “free from panel size and resolution constraints,” according to LG Display, which means it can be used for virtually any panel requirements, including VR and AR displays.
LG Display says it will start by applying this technology to “IT applications,” such as tablets and monitors, before later expanding to cover products like ultra-large TVs and 1-inch wearable devices. There’s no word on when production will start, or when the first products will be available to buy.
summary: LG Display has introduced a new OLED manufacturing method called FLiPP that eliminates the need for fine metal masks. This technology uses photolithography and UV light to pattern pixels, resulting in displays that are brighter, more energy-efficient, longer-lasting, and virtually free from size constraints. LG plans to apply FLiPP initially to IT applications like tablets and monitors before expanding to other devices.
key_points: LG Display unveiled the FLiPP (FMM-Less innovative Pixel Patterning) manufacturing method.
FLiPP eliminates fine metal masks (FMM) by using photolithography and UV light.
The technology makes OLED panels 1.6 times brighter, 2.4 times longer-lasting, and 13 percent more energy-efficient.
FLiPP removes panel size and resolution constraints, making it suitable for devices ranging from VR and AR displays to ultra-large TVs.
LG will initially apply the technology to IT applications such as tablets and monitors.

title: Stupid Never Dies – a zombie fights for the love of a frozen corpse
author: Bex April May
content:
Love is blind. In Stupid Never Dies, it is also frozen solid and technically dead as Davy, the weakest zombie in monster society, discovers Julia’s body in a shopping centre and falls in love at first sight. He wants to bring her back to life and take her on a date. Unfortunately, that means defeating the King of Monsters (KOM) and accidentally saving humanity along the way.
This is the gloriously ridiculous setup for this forthcoming action RPG from GPTrack50, a new studio founded by former Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi. Its world looks much like ours, except that monsters have always been part of everyday life: whereas we might find a bear in the mountains or a stray dog in the woods, residents here encounter werewolves and zombies.
![Five figures in a row inside a mall: a female zombie on a motorbike, a gargoyle in a shopping trolley, the male zombie protagonist, a man with pointy ears and wolf-like feet, and a young woman holding a weapon adapted from a broom.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/faa27a4325342551975abdc59f27259802273dff/0_0_3840_2160/master/3840.png?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That uneasy normality ends when KOM crushes civilisation and leaves only 2% of humanity alive. Davy begins even lower down the social ladder. Zombies, says Kobayashi, are “the weakest of the weak”. But eating a mysterious egg gives this particularly unimpressive corpse the power to fight back.
Because Davy is already dead, combat throws out the usual need for self-preservation. Forget defence: guarding and dodging are pushed aside in favour of “attacking, attacking, attacking”. Kobayashi describes it as a game made “by the action game lover, for the action gamer”.
![A frenetic fight scene featuring multiple enemies with health bars above their heads.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/a21527e3f408876a39e258f2ee6dd050a257235d/0_0_3840_2160/master/3840.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Its two main systems make full use of Davy’s unreliable body. He can consume defeated monsters, steal their skills and transform into creatures including a werewolf, vampire or harpy. The “body hack” mechanic goes further, allowing players to replace his head, arms and legs with equipment. Attach a sword to an arm and Davy gains sword attacks; fit a gun and he starts shooting. Being undead has never looked so practical.
Kobayashi calls the result “funky zombie action”, a phrase coined to give the development team a shared idea of the game’s tone: fast, colourful and darkly funny. It also captures the freedom Kobayashi found after years working on some of the world’s most famous franchises, including Resident Evil and Devil May Cry.
Large franchises bring large audiences and expectations. A new studio making a new IP had neither. As Kobayashi says, “We don’t have a fan yet.” That has allowed its team of around 30 developers, many recruited from companies including Capcom, Konami and Square Enix, to use stranger jokes and sharper humour than they ever could when working on those older series.
The studio itself began almost as scrappily as Davy. In its early months, GPTrack50 had programmers and designers but no artists, so the team bought outside assets to build a rough white-box prototype. Around 20 external companies eventually joined the three-year production, drawn, Kobayashi says, by the chance to create something completely from scratch. He hopes players finish thinking: “This is the experience that I was looking for. This is a new thing.”
Underneath the monster-eating and gun-limbs is a simple underdog story: Davy rises from the bottom of monster society to challenge its king, but he is not driven by glory. Saving the remaining humans is almost incidental, as Kobayashi explains: “He wants to go out for a date [with] this frozen girl.”
Romance isn’t dead; it just needs defrosting.
summary: Stupid Never Dies is an upcoming action RPG from developer GPTrack50, founded by former Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi. The game follows Davy, a weak zombie who falls in love with a frozen human corpse and must defeat the King of Monsters to take her on a date. Combat emphasizes relentless attacking, monster consumption for transformation, and replacing Davy's body parts with weapons and equipment. Operating as a new intellectual property allows the team of roughly 30 developers to embrace a fast, colorful, and darkly funny tone without the constraints of major legacy franchises.
key_points: The game is developed by GPTrack50, a new studio founded by former Capcom producer Hiroyuki Kobayashi.
The protagonist Davy is a weak zombie who fights the King of Monsters to revive and date a frozen human corpse, accidentally saving humanity in the process.
Combat mechanics allow Davy to consume defeated monsters to gain their skills and replace his body parts with equipment like swords and guns.
Being a new IP with no pre-existing fan expectations has given the 30-person development team the freedom to use stranger jokes and sharper, darkly funny humor.

title: The big three US carriers are offering some Pixel 11 models for free, here is what you need to know
author: Peter
content:
The Google Pixel 11 series is now available in stores and from carriers in select regions, following a week of pre-orders. Here’s a look at what the big three US carriers have to offer.
T-Mobile is offering the three non-folding models for free – or as the carrier puts it “get the Pixel 11 Pro XL on Us”. This means that it’s $1,300 off, making the base model free. You need to add a new line or trade in an old device (in any condition) and sign up for Experience Beyond 2.0 and Go5G Next. The actual discount will come in the form of credits to your monthly bill (up to 36 months).
Similarly, the Pixel 11 and 11 Pro are available with Essentials 2.0 and Experience More 2.0/Go5G Plus, respectively. The Google Pixel Watch 5 is $300 off, so a 41mm model will cost you $200 and a 45mm model is $30 more. You’ll need to add a new line on the Watch Plus Plan for that.
T-Mobile also has a 25% discount on an accessory bundle – a case, a screen protector and a charger. Business users are also looking at free devices (“on Us”), check the press release for more details. Note that some plans give you access to T-Satellite, which is a T-Mobile/SpaceX collaboration that adds cell coverage via Starlink satellites.
AT&T offers the Google Pixel 11 Pro for free if you trade in an old Pixel – it can be any old Pixel phone in any condition. The Pro XL model has a similar deal – up to $1,350 off with a trade-in. The vanilla Pixel 11, meanwhile, is available for $11/month with no trade-in required. The Pixel Watch 5 is 50% off when purchased online.
The Pixel 11 series is FirstNet Ready (this is a government-run network for first responders). The phones are available for AT&T Business customers too, more details here.
Existing Verizon customers can get up to $900 off on an eligible myPlan by trading in an old phone. This makes the vanilla Pixel 11 free. If you want the Pixel 11 Pro (256GB), you can get it for $45 a month for 48 months – this means a $15 device payment plus a $30 plan rate per month. $15 x 48 months = $720, so this includes $380 in promotional credits.
If you don’t want to get locked into using the Pro for four years, you can get it for free on the Simplicity plan for $80 a month – this plan allows you to upgrade your phone every year. Verizon Business users can get up to $900 off on the Pixel 11 series – more on that in the press release.
The Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold is available on T-Mobile and Verizon (but not on AT&T), but you won’t be getting any special deals and discounts for it.

title: iPhone 18 Pro launches soon: From price to release date, here’s everything to know
author: Alex Lee
content:
Next month, Apple will host its big September spectacle and, with it, the launch of the tech giant’s iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. For months now, rumours and leaks have been giving us an insight into the company’s latest flagship phones.
The new release is expected to feature the best camera on any iPhone, with many insiders predicting the smartphone to boast a DSLR-like variable aperture, giving you precise, manual control over the background blur. A new leak has also shone a light on the phone’s upcoming specs.
With Apple reportedly punting the regular iPhone 18 to next year, all eyes are currently on the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and the long-rumoured iPhone Ultra. Here's everything we know so far.
Read more: Best refurbished iPhone deals
Latest iPhone 18 Pro news and rumours
We’ve not really heard too much about the iPhone 18 Pro’s specs, but some rumours are starting to trickle in. Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital has claimed that Apple’s A20 Pro chip could be 18 per cent faster than the A19 Pro, though could be more expensive to manufacture.
According to the leaker, the A20 Pro is rumoured to use TSMC’s new 2nm manufacturing process, with a new transistor design known as GAA. This should mean Apple can squeeze more performance out of the chip without using more power. If true, it should make the phone more efficient, with Fixed Focus Digital claiming it’ll consume up to 30 per cent less power than the A19 Pro.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro release date
The release timeline for the iPhone 18 and subsequent iPhones could look a lot different going forward. In late 2025, the ever-reliable Apple insider Mark Gurman claimed that the company will be moving away from its annual autumnal launch extravaganza. Instead, Gurman claimed it will be spreading its iPhone launches throughout the year.
According to Gurman, the reason for the shift is that Apple’s decision to cram everything into September has become burdensome. It gives the company fewer opportunities to spread out revenue across the year, while also straining its marketing and engineering teams and overloading suppliers.
So Apple’s predicted to shake up its launch window entirely. Gurman says we won’t be seeing the regular iPhone 18 unveiled in September this year. Instead, Apple will only launch the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, as well as its first foldable phone.
The tech giant is then predicted to launch the regular iPhone 18 in the spring of 2027, alongside the iPhone 18e. There’s precedent for this – we’ve just seen Apple launch the iPhone 17e in March, for example. Gurman says the brand could also launch a follow-up to the iPhone Air.
As for the actual release date of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, that’s still fairly easy to predict, given that the date of Apple’s September spectacle isn’t expected to change.
Apple almost always announces its new line of smartphones in the second week of September. To give you an idea, the iPhone 17 was announced on Tuesday 9 September 2025, the iPhone 16 was announced on Monday 9 September 2024, the iPhone 15 on Tuesday 5 September 2023, the iPhone 14 on Wednesday 7 September 2022 and the iPhone 13 on Tuesday 14 September 2021.
Labor Day in the US is on Monday 7 September this year, so Apple is unlikely to unveil its latest launches then. I’m expecting Apple to show off the iPhone 18 Pro on either Tuesday 8 September or Wednesday 9 September – most likely the latter, with pre-orders going live on Friday 11 September. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported in late June that he also believed the iPhone 18 Pro would be unveiled on one of those dates.
The iPhone 18 Pro could then be released on Friday 18 September. However, it might be tricky to acquire if the latest rumours are to be believed.
Former Bloomberg reporter Tim Culpan claims that Apple and its suppliers are scrambling to procure enough memory chips for its upcoming iPhones.
Culpan says that “assemblers are working with Apple to rush shipments of DRAM used in mobile devices”, adding that Apple relies heavily on chip manufacturer Micron for DRAM, but also procures from SK Hynix and Samsung.
That could mean the iPhone 18 Pro will be in even shorter supply than normal when it launches in September, especially if the tech giant isn’t able to manufacture as many smartphones as it would like. A month out and production should ordinarily be full steam ahead by now, with Apple building up stock ahead of one of its biggest launches of the year.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro price
While I always take price increases with a grain of salt, when it comes from Tim Cook himself, it’s no longer just a rumour.
On 17 June, in an interview with The Wall Street Journal, Cook warned that a price hike would be unavoidable. “We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us, and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation has become unsustainable,” he said.
A week later, Apple raised prices of the iPad, MacBook, HomePod and Apple TV in the UK. Apple’s entire range of iPads increased by up to £200, the MacBook by up to £300, the HomePod by up to £50 and the Apple TV 4K by up to £100. It’s not a good sign for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, which are both expected to house even more RAM to power Apple Intelligence
Analysts are now predicting a price hike for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. A recent Financial Times report is claiming that Apple is racing to secure more RAM from two Chinese chip manufacturers – ChangXin Memory Technologies and Yangtze Memory Technologies. The report claims Apple is lobbying the US government to allow the company to buy the chips from the two state-backed companies, who are blacklisted by the Pentagon, with the Chinese-made phones potentially being limited to China.
However, it may be too late to help lower the cost of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, according to Apple analysts Ming-Chi Kuo, the DRAM shortage will continue to widen into 2027.
Samsung notably increased the price of the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra earlier this year by £30. Apple’s price hike could be even steeper. Analytics firm IDC expects Apple to increase the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max by $100 in the US. Given devices in the UK received the same nominal increase as the US last week, that would translate to a £100 price hike.
The iPhone 17 Pro cost £1,099 at launch, while the iPhone 17 Pro Max launched for £1,199.
This contrasts with what analysts have been saying all year, however, with analysts previously suggesting Apple will absorb any extra costs. Jeff Pu of GF Securities previously stated that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will cost the same as the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max. In a February 2026 research note obtained by MacRumours, Pu said Apple was looking at keeping the prices the same or similar by focusing on “cost management”.
In the research note, Pu said Apple had been negotiating with Samsung and SK Hynix to achieve relatively “favourable” memory chip deals, and was looking to lower the costs of other parts, such as the camera and display.
The pricing prediction was first raised by the ever-reliable Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, who said in January that Apple was looking to keep the price of the iPhone 18 Pro the same as the previous generation.
On 12 May, MacRumors published a report claiming that Pu expected Apple to outperform in the smartphone market with an “aggressive pricing strategy” for the iPhone 18 Pro. Pu previously predicted that the starting prices of the iPhone 18 Pro models would either remain unchanged from the iPhone 17 Pro lineup or only increase slightly.
That prediction has seemingly changed in recent weeks. The latest report from Pu has poured a bucket of ice-cold water on any hopes of an affordable iPhone this September.
He now reports that the iPhone 18 Pro could come with a $250-$300 price hike, which translates to roughly £185-£220 in the UK. If true, that could mean the iPhone 18 Pro starts from £1,299, making it the most expensive iPhone Pro ever.
Pu claims this is due to the rising cost of 2nm silicon and DRAM/NAND, with Apple passing those costs on to consumers.
In late July, it was revealed that Apple is reportedly racing to secure cheaper components in a bid to offset the price of RAM, which could help keep down the cost of the next iPhone. Korean-based outlet The Elec reported that Apple is pushing Samsung Display and LG Display to supply its OLED panels for $70 each, but that it could get it even lower than that.
The Elec says Apple may get its new OLED panels for just $66.50, which would be a 20 percent reduction compared to the price paid for the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
While The Elec says that the cost of displays has gone down every year, the reduction Apple is seeking is unusually steep. By bringing down the cost of other components, Apple might be able to produce its next iPhone more cheaply, meaning the price hike to you could also be less.
Apple iPhone 18 design and display
While the iPhone 17 Pro looked dramatically different to the iPhone 16 Pro, leakers right now are predicting the iPhone 18 Pro will look fairly similar to the iPhone 17 Pro. The biggest design change is that the Dynamic Island will be shrunk slightly, so that it doesn’t take up as much screen real estate.
In January this year, leaker Ice Universe claimed the Dynamic Island will be 35 per cent narrower than the current version, with a width of around 13.5mm, down from 20.7mm. The leaker shared a mock-up of what that could look like. Ice Universe’s track record has been fairly good for Samsung leaks, but a bit mixed when it comes to Apple.
Earlier rumours suggested Apple was testing a smaller hole-punch cutout instead of a Dynamic Island, with Face ID moving under the screen. This would give the iPhone a screen without interruptions for the first time. However, in January 2026, Weibo leaker Instant Digital stated this had been a mistranslation, and that there would be no hole-punch cutout instead of a Dynamic Island or under-the-screen Face ID.
Instead, the Face ID flood illuminator is the only component that will be moved under the screen, because it’s relatively small. Display industry analyst Ross Young claims Apple will keep this smaller Dynamic Island until at least 2027.
Several leakers have since backed up Ice Universe’s claim. In late March, X account Early Apple shared a supposed prototype image of the iPhone 18 Pro with a shrunken Dynamic Island. The camera flash also appears to illuminate a faint circular area on the display, hinting at the Face ID flood illuminator being hidden under the screen.
Ice Universe also claimed in late March that the bezels on the iPhone 18 series will remain the same as the iPhone 17 and iPhone 16, while reiterating that the Dynamic Island will be smaller.
Another interesting rumour from Instant Digital is that the iPhone 18 Pro Max could be slightly thicker than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and could weigh roughly 243g. If true, it would make it the heaviest iPhone Apple’s ever produced. That’s 10g heavier than the iPhone 17 Pro Max and 3g heavier than the iPhone 14 Pro Max (the current heavyweight record holder).
Other than that, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max could look similar to the previous models, boasting 6.3in and 6.9in displays as well as a triple-lens system with the plateau design introduced on the iPhone 17 Pro.
On 22 April, tech YouTuber Vadim Yuryev shared images of dummy units of the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro Max. And if accurate, it doesn’t look like it’s going to be very different to the iPhone 17 Pro Max. But look a little harder, and you’ll notice that the cameras are a lot thicker, with Yuryev stating the black glass on the cameras protrudes a lot more too.
Why is this? According to long-held rumours, the camera is going to get a massive upgrade in September, with Apple implementing variable aperture for the first time and improved sensors.
The first iPhone 18 Pro dummy unit surfaced in late May and early June, giving us a better look at the dark cherry iPhone colourway. While these are just dummy units, they line up with the predicted colour scheme, and come courtesy of TechDroider Clips on YouTube and a Weibo leaker.
In early May, South Korean publication The Elec reported that the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max could boast advanced LTPO+ OLED panels supplied by Samsung Display and LG Display. The upgraded screens are said to be more power efficient, which could help boost battery life, while also being less susceptible to burn-in.
On 29 June, Reuters revealed that more than 200,000 files stolen from Apple's manufacturing partner Tata Electronics had been leaked on the dark web. The leaked archive included supplier lists, engineering documents, component specifications and photos and videos showing the unreleased iPhone 18 Pro undergoing drop testing. It could be the biggest Apple supply chain breach to date.
Cybersecurity researchers say the stolen data began appearing on the dark web on 10 June, but Tata Electronics hadn’t reported the data breach until 22 June. In the leaked videos and images, a drop test of a smartphone with a three-camera layout and Apple logo can be seen. Last week, AppleInsider reported that board layouts for the iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max were also contained in the data breach, as well as a data sheet for the upcoming A18 Pro chip.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro colours
One interesting decision Apple made for the iPhone 17 Pro was to give the handsets a two-tone design. Controversially, the glass back for MagSafe charging is a different colour to the aluminium frame, making it look less uniform. Apple is reportedly looking to reduce this contrast for the iPhone 18 Pro.
In November 2025, Instant Digital reported that Apple had changed the phone’s back glass process to help minimise the two-tone look seen on the iPhone 17 Pro, giving the phones a more unified look.
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/04/16/9/18/iphone-18-deep-red.png)
In late February, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also claimed that Apple was testing a deep red colour for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Fold. On 11 April, Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed the same, based on the fact the insider has seen prototypes of Android phones in the same deep red colour.
On 1 May, Macworld claimed a source familiar with Apple’s supply chain had information regarding the colourways for the upcoming smartphones. According to the publication, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will come in a dark cherry colourway, which it says will be “much closer to wine than fruit punch”. It says that Apple has also been experimenting with a light blue colourway, similar to the iPhone 17’s mist blue, as well as a dark grey. There will also reportedly be a silver colourway to complete the line-up.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro cameras
Of all the features to receive the biggest shake-up, it’s almost always the camera system
In December 2024, Ming-Chi Kuo claimed the main rear camera on the iPhone 18 Pro will feature variable aperture for the first time, making it act more like a DSLR camera. Variable aperture would enable iPhone users to control how much light comes through the lens. Kuo claimed Dutch manufacturer BE Semiconductor would supply the assembly equipment used to produce the aperture blades.
Several reputable leakers have since corroborated this leak in recent months, with ETNews the latest to do so, in October 2025. The iPhones have had fixed apertures for years, so this could be a significant upgrade.
Apple is also reportedly testing a new telephoto camera for the iPhone 18 Pro. Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station claimed in October last year that the telephoto lens will also feature a larger aperture, being upgraded from the iPhone 17 Pro’s f/2.8 telephoto lens.
Another (fairly old) leak, from January 2025, comes from Taiwanese publication DigiTimes. The publication claimed that Samsung has developed a new three-layer stacked camera sensor system specifically for the iPhone 18. According to DigiTimes, this would make the iPhone 18’s cameras more responsive and reduce noise.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro specs
Spec details for the iPhone 18 Pro are still fairly thin on the ground, but several leaks suggest Apple’s next-generation A20 chip will power the devices.
According to Jeff Pu, the A20 chip is expected to use TSMC’s new 2nm manufacturing process, which could make it up to 15 per cent faster and 30 per cent more efficient than the current A19 chip.
An August 2025 report from Ming-Chi Kuo also suggests the A20 could use a new chip packaging method that integrates RAM directly with the processor, potentially improving performance for Apple Intelligence features, while freeing up space inside the phone.
Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman also claims iPhone 18 Pro models will feature Apple’s next-generation C2 modem. The chip is expected to improve 5G performance and could add support for mmWave connectivity, bringing it closer to the Qualcomm modems Apple currently uses. Weibo leaker Fixed Digital also suggested, in February 2026, that it could support new satellite connectivity standards, potentially allowing for full internet access over satellite networks when traditional coverage isn’t available.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro battery
In early July, new regulatory certification filings from China were discovered by Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station purporting to show the battery capacity for both the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max.
According to the filings in China's C3 database, the iPhone 18 Pro Max will have a 4,056mAh battery in China, while the US eSIM-only handset will get a 4,288mAh battery. That’s slightly up on the 3,988mAh and 4,252mAh battery capacity for the iPhone 17 Pro. The iPhone 18 Pro Max will reportedly getting a much bigger battery life boost, however.
The filing says the iPhone 18 Pro Max will boast a 5,391mAh battery in China, with the eSIM-only model in the US getting a 5,567mAh battery. That’s a huge jump on the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 4,823mAh battery in China and the 5,088mAh battery in the US. In comparison, the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra has a 5,000mAh battery.
I’ll be rounding up all the latest leaks right here on this page as more rumours come in, so stay tuned.
The best iPhone 17 Pro carrier deals
Don’t want to wait months to get your hands on a new iPhone? The iPhone 17 Pro is a splendid phone and, right now, it doesn’t look like the upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro will be massive. Below, we’ve rounded up some of the best iPhone 17 Pro carrier deals in the UK.
![Apple claims the iPhone 17 Pro Max can last up to 39 hours on a single charge](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/09/10/15/50/iphone-17-pro-orange.png)
Affordable Mobiles currently has one of the cheapest iPhone 17 Pro deals. You can get the phone with 100GB of data for £49 per month and a £39 up-front cost. The deal is with mobile network Three, meaning you get access to Three+ rewards and free wifi on the London underground.
![If you’ve bought a new iPhone in the last five years, you’re in luck](https://static.independent.co.uk/2025/09/15/8/24/iOS-26-IndyBest.jpg)
Mobile Phones Direct currently has one of the best iPhone 17 Pro Max deals right now. You can get the iPhone 17 Pro Max with unlimited data for £58 per month with the Three network. You have to pay £69 up-front, but it’s a decent monthly price for an unlimited contract.
For more, we’ve reviewed the latest iPhone 17e to see if it’s worth the price tag
summary: Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in September, featuring potential upgrades like an A20 Pro chip, a DSLR-like variable aperture camera, and a slightly smaller Dynamic Island. However, production may face supply constraints due to ongoing DRAM shortages. Analysts predict a price increase for the new lineup ranging from $100 to $300, driven by rising component costs.
key_points: The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to be announced in September, while the regular iPhone 18 may launch in spring 2027.
Rumored specs include an A20 Pro chip built on a 2nm process, a variable aperture camera system, and a Dynamic Island that is about 35 per cent narrower.
Apple is facing component shortages and rising manufacturing costs for RAM and silicon, which CEO Tim Cook indicated will lead to unavoidable price hikes.
Analysts predict potential price increases for the iPhone 18 Pro models, ranging from $100 up to $300 depending on the source.

title: The Duskbloods Gameplay Has Leaked Ahead Of Network Test
author: Nintendo Life; Ollie Reynolds
content:
![The Duskbloods](https://images.nintendolife.com/cac5c37bf5c59/the-duskbloods.900x.jpg)
FromSoftware is getting ready to kick off its network test for The Duskbloods this weekend, but it looks like a gameplay video has leaked ahead of time.
WARNING: descriptive spoilers of the footage to follow.
We're not going to embed or provide a link to the footage here, but needless to say, it's not particularly difficult to find. Uploaded to Bilibili, the video can now be found all over social media and YouTube, and depicts a 3v3 multiplayer fight called the 'Grail Battle', or 'Moon Blood Bestowal'.
Here's the brief description from the loading screen:
"The final battle, on the night of dusk.
"The grail beckons three Bloodsworn, but the moontears will flow for one and one alone."
The battle itself takes place on a rooftop with what looks to be a pool of blood in its centre. The entire scene is bathed in the red glow of the moon while our participants duke it out. It seems each is able to call upon a summon ally to aid in battle, with players also able to transform periodically to execute special attacks.
The gameplay looks very fast and frantic, combining Bloodborne's dodge mechanic with Elden Ring's ability to jump at will. One the battle is over, a message appears onscreen to proclaim "You are the Victor of this Dusk". Pretty cool.
We don't have long to wait now until we can experience The Duskbloods for ourselves. The network test kicks off on Friday for all successful participants, and if you want to know specific timings, then check out our full guide for more information.
summary: Gameplay footage of FromSoftware's upcoming game The Duskbloods has leaked online ahead of this weekend's network test. The leaked video shows a 3v3 multiplayer match featuring fast-paced combat, rooftop settings, summon allies, and character transformations. The network test for successful participants is scheduled to kick off on Friday.
key_points: A gameplay video for The Duskbloods leaked on Bilibili and spread across social media and YouTube ahead of the network test.
The leaked footage depicts a 3v3 multiplayer fight known as the 'Grail Battle' or 'Moon Blood Bestowal'.
Combat mechanics shown include a fast-paced rooftop fight combining Bloodborne's dodge with Elden Ring's jumping ability.
Players can call upon summon allies and periodically transform to execute special attacks.
The official network test begins this weekend on Friday for successful participants.

title: Google releases Pixel 11 series factory images
author: Abner Li
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/08/Pixel-11-family-1.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
With the Pixel 11 series hitting store shelves today, Google has released factory images for all the devices.
There are three builds for each phone:
- CD1A.260618.001.A7
- CD1A.260618.001.C2
- CD1A.260714.001.A9
This is Android 17 (not QPR1) with the August 2026 security patch. Google has not specified which carrier or region each build corresponds to. We’re on A9 in the US (on Google Fi).
These images help you restore a software-damaged phone to the original factory firmware. Google says it is “typically easier and safer to sideload the full OTA image instead,” which are also available today.
Today’s additions confirm that bears are the codename theme this generation:
- Pixel 11: cubs
- Pixel 11 Pro: grizzly
- Pixel 11 Pro XL: kodiak
- Pixel 11 Pro Fold: yogi
As of today, the Pixel 11 series is not eligible for Android 17 QPR1 or QPR2 via the Android Beta Program.
![Add 9to5Google as a preferred source on Google](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/themes/ninetofive/dist/images/google-preferred-source-badge-dark.png) 
![Add 9to5Google as a preferred source on Google](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/themes/ninetofive/dist/images/google-preferred-source-badge-light.png)
summary: Google has released factory images and full OTA images for the newly launched Pixel 11 series devices as they hit store shelves. The software features Android 17 with the August 2026 security patch across three different builds. Additionally, the releases confirm that the internal codename theme for this generation of Pixel devices is bears.
key_points: Factory and full OTA images are available for the Pixel 11 series on its release day.
Three distinct builds are provided for each phone running Android 17 with the August 2026 security patch.
The bear-themed codenames for the generation are cubs for the Pixel 11, grizzly for the Pro, kodiak for the Pro XL, and yogi for the Pro Fold.
The Pixel 11 series is not currently eligible for Android 17 QPR1 or QPR2 via the Android Beta Program.

title: Sennheiser’s new Momentum 5 earbuds feature easily replaceable batteries
author: Andrew Liszewski
content:
Sennheiser announced the next version of its flagship wireless earbuds with a major redesign focusing on sustainability. The company claims the new design improves the Momentum True Wireless 5’s “comfort, stability, and portability,” but a more compelling reason to upgrade is that you won’t have to replace them in a few years when they stop holding a charge. Both the Momentum 5 earbuds and their charging case feature user-replaceable batteries that are accessible using a compact screwdriver instead of having to hack through layers of glue.
Sennheiser’s new Momentum 5 earbuds feature easily replaceable batteries
A screwdriver is all you’ll need to swap a new battery into the Momentum 5’s charging case and earbuds.
![sennheiser2](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/sennheiser2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.0099980003999178%2C100%2C99.9800039992&w=2400)
![sennheiser2](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/sennheiser2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0.0099980003999178%2C100%2C99.9800039992&w=2400)
The Momentum True Wireless 5 will be available starting on September 3rd for $299.95, which is the same price as the Momentum 4 that launched in early 2024. Color options include five metallic finishes: lavender, copper, denim, graphite, and cream.
![The full metallic color lineup of the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 earbuds.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/08/sennheiser1.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0%2C0%2C100%2C100&w=2400)
Replaceable batteries are becoming more common in devices again thanks in part to European sustainability regulations that will go into effect in early 2027. Sennheiser and other companies like Fender and Glorious now offer larger over-ear headphones with swappable batteries, but adoption has been slow for earbuds that are typically assembled using glue to make them as small and light as possible.
Bang & Olufsen’s Beoplay Eleven earbuds launched in late 2024 with replaceable batteries, but users need to send them in so a professional technician can do the swap. Other earbuds allow users to replace the battery in the charging case, but the Momentum 5 join the Fairphone Fairbuds as one of the few options where users can replace the buds’ batteries themselves. On top of that, the Momentum 5’s battery life has been boosted to up to 12 hours per charge, or up to 40 in total when paired with the Qi-compatible and now slimmer charging case. The Momentum 4 topped out at 7.5 hours alone, or up to 30 hours with their case.
Other improvements include a redesigned ear tip that works alongside a revised adaptive ANC system to improve noise canceling, and support for Dolby Atmos and spatial audio with the addition of interactive head tracking. Sennheiser also claims the Momentum 5 will offer more stable wireless connections with support for Bluetooth 6.0 and a “robust mode” that improves connectivity in environments with a lot of interference.
summary: Sennheiser has announced the Momentum True Wireless 5 earbuds, featuring a sustainability-focused redesign with user-replaceable batteries in both the buds and the charging case. Available on September 3rd for $299.95, the new model offers a redesigned fit, improved battery life of up to 12 hours, and enhanced noise cancellation. Additional updates include Bluetooth 6.0 support, spatial audio with interactive head tracking, and five metallic color options.
key_points: Both the Momentum 5 earbuds and their charging case feature user-replaceable batteries accessible with a compact screwdriver.
The earbuds launch on September 3rd for $299.95 in five metallic color finishes.
Battery life is boosted to up to 12 hours per charge, with a total of 40 hours using the slimmer, Qi-compatible charging case.
New features include Bluetooth 6.0, spatial audio with interactive head tracking, and improved adaptive active noise cancellation.

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta may have eradicated the annoying 'Compiling Shaders' wait PC players loathe
author: Sherif Saed
content:
While sharing the remaining details about the upcoming Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta scheduled for this weekend - such as pre-load information and PC specs - Infinity Ward and co-developer Beenox have revealed an unexpected PC gaming breakthrough. It's to do with eliminating elongated wait times associated with compiling a game's shaders.
In a wide-ranging blog post, the Call of Duty developers discussed their solution to the 'Compiling Shaders' issue most PC players should be familiar with. This isn't isolated to just Call of Duty games; it's so widespread it's a surprise when a game doesn't have it.
To recap, modern games on PC require shaders to tell your graphics card how to render what you see on screen. By compiling shaders for things like effects, lighting, shadows and surfaces ahead of time, the game doesn't have to struggle in the moment when these are called on during play.
The problem is that compiling shaders can take time, and that it has to be done in full when you start a game for the first time, after you update your GPU drivers, and when major patches are released. Consoles do not have this problem, since their downloads come with shaders included, due to their standardised hardware and software configurations.
But starting with the Modern Warfare 4 beta, Call of Duty games are now capable of pre-loading shaders before you load them up. Once the download is complete, shaders start pre-loading in the background, though this comes with a few caveats.
For now, the Battle.net launcher appears to be the optimal way to experience this tech during the beta, because it's the only place shader pre-loading begins by default. On Steam, shader pre-loading is enabled, but you'll need to sit through the 'Compiling Shaders' step still, the first time you start the game - though it should be faster. Any time you launch the game in the future, shader pre-loading should achieve the intended effect.
This is a notable first step, but the real benefits of this new tech won't be felt until Modern Warfare 4's full release, as that's when PC players need to compile shaders once, without having to do so each major seasonal update, as is the case today.
![Cover image for YouTube video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/qeFVhw4YNbM/hqdefault.jpg) Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 | Multiplayer Trailer
The Modern Warfare 4 beta is also addressing another long-standing PC technical issue: the 'Update Requires Restart' phenomenon, which Call of Duty players should be very familiar with.
When launching on PC and consoles, the game checks for updates, and if it finds one, it installs it - a process which requires a game restart before it takes effect. In certain cases, updates are not applied together, meaning you may have to repeat this process several times before you can actually play. This is common when returning to a Call of Duty game you haven't played in a while.
Starting with the Modern Warfare 4 beta, Infinity Ward is reducing the number of instances in which this is going to happen. In simple terms, the developer is making it so more types of patches can be downloaded without the need for a restart.
That change won't affect all cases; if an update arrives as you're playing and you get kicked out, a restart will still be required. But the goal is that those instances are rarer.
Much like the shader situation, the update has a few quirks of its own. PC players - regardless of the store they bought the game from - should get the intended experience. PlayStation 5 players likewise receive the fix. Xbox players, however, are still required to restart to apply an update, but the developer is working to reduce these situations for the game's full release. The only platform to not benefit from that work is, unfortunately, Nintendo Switch 2, where restarts continue to be required during both beta and launch.
"While 'Update Requires Restart' isn't disappearing completely, the goal is simple: fewer required restarts and fewer interruptions between you and your next match," the developer said.
The first leg of the Modern Warfare 4 beta begins tomorrow, 21st August, immediately following the conclusion of Call of Duty: Next, the live event where much of the beta's maps and modes will be shown. Pre-loading kicks off today at 9am PT / 12pm ET / 5pm BST. If you're on PC, make sure to enable TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot, as they're both required to play.
summary: Infinity Ward and Beenox have introduced a new technology for the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta that aims to eliminate the lengthy 'Compiling Shaders' wait times traditionally experienced by PC players. The developers are also addressing the annoying 'Update Requires Restart' issue by reducing the number of patches that force a game restart on certain platforms. These technical improvements begin rolling out with the beta starting on August 21st, with full benefits expected upon the game's complete release.
key_points: Call of Duty developers have introduced background shader pre-loading to eliminate elongated 'Compiling Shaders' wait times on PC.
The Battle.net launcher is currently the optimal way to experience shader pre-loading by default during the beta.
The Modern Warfare 4 beta is reducing instances of the 'Update Requires Restart' phenomenon, allowing more patches to apply without a restart.
PlayStation 5 and PC players will benefit from the reduced restart update process during the beta, while Xbox and Nintendo Switch 2 users have different current limitations.
The Modern Warfare 4 beta begins on August 21st, with pre-loading starting at 9am PT / 12pm ET / 5pm BST, and requires TPM 2.0 and Secure Boot on PC.

title: PS5 Fighting Game 2XKO Throws in the Towel, Just Can't Get Enough Players
author: Push Square; Robert Ramsey
content:
![2XKO Ending Development](https://images.pushsquare.com/5f34b038eacad/2xko-ending-development.900x.jpg)
The live service space is brutal — and I imagine that cracking it is even harder when you're a fighting game.
Fairly high expectations were placed upon 2XKO when it was first announced and eventually released into early access on PC. A free-to-play fighting game felt like a bold step forward for the genre — and being based on League of Legends, it had serious weight behind it in terms of brand recognition.
But it just never seemed to stick. The tag brawler released for PS5 in January of this year, and it was only a matter of weeks before we heard about the development team being downsized.
Despite Riot Games reassuring players that it would remain focused on adding to and improving 2XKO, the writing was on the wall. If it couldn't start attracting more players at a relatively rapid pace, then it wouldn't last.
Unfortunately, it sounds like the numbers simply never increased. And now, Riot Games has confirmed that active development on 2XKO will cease at the end of 2026.
A refreshingly transparent statement from the team reads:
"Over the last few months, we’ve been monitoring 2XKO’s trajectory closely, and what we’ve seen is painting a clear, consistent picture: while a lot of you jumped in to try the game and there's an incredible community that plays every day, we haven’t seen enough players stick with the game to get to a path toward sustainability."
It should be stressed that 2XKO will remain online for the foreseeable future — it's not getting shut down or anything like that. It just won't be receiving any additional support in the form of updates and DLC.
A "final bug fix patch" will drop in December, and that'll be that.
summary: Riot Games has announced that active development on the free-to-play fighting game 2XKO will cease at the end of 2026 due to an inability to maintain a sustainable player base. Although the game experienced early interest following its PC early access and subsequent PS5 release in January, player numbers did not increase enough over time. However, the game will remain online for the foreseeable future, with a final bug fix patch scheduled for December.
key_points: Active development on 2XKO will cease at the end of 2026.
Riot Games cited a lack of player retention and sustainability as the primary reason for ending development.
The game will remain online for the foreseeable future without receiving further updates or DLC.
A final bug fix patch is scheduled to be released in December.

title: "The release date is inaccurate" - No, The Duskbloods isn't releasing on 24th September, according to Nintendo
author: Connor Makar
content:
Nintendo has denied that The Duskbloods will be releasing on the 24th September, after the date was included in an early preview of the game.
This date was featured at the end of The Guardian's preview coverage, written as part of a trip to Tokyo to play it in advance of this weekend's upcoming network test.
![Cover image for YouTube video](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dMrTr9cz53k/hqdefault.jpg) The Duskbloods - Official Closed Network Test Trailer | Nintendo Direct June 2026
Curiously, other publications seemingly on the trip do not include the release date, instead stating it will be released later this year. Eurogamer contacted Nintendo to confirm the validity of this date, and received this response from an official spokesperson from Nintendo:
"The release date is inaccurate because there is no information regarding [the] release date of the Duskbloods."
This date-reveal comes one day before a closed network test, which members of the public were able to sign up for following a Nintendo Direct trailer last month. It also comes as leaked gameplay footage appeared online earlier today, which was re-uploaded to social media platform Bilibili before being taken down again.
If you need help seeing if you've got access to The Duskbloods network test, you can read Eurogamer's guide here which breaks down all the steps.
summary: Nintendo has clarified that the September 24th release date for The Duskbloods is inaccurate, stating that no official release date has been announced. The date had appeared in an early preview by The Guardian following a press trip to Tokyo. Meanwhile, the game is preparing for a closed network test ahead of its planned launch later this year.
key_points: Nintendo stated that the release date of September 24th for The Duskbloods is inaccurate.
The date was originally published in an early preview by The Guardian.
Other publications on the same press trip reported that the game will release later this year.
A closed network test for the game is scheduled to begin shortly.
Leaked gameplay footage recently surfaced online before being taken down.

title: Yes, the Pixelsnap magnets on Pixel 11 are stronger this year
author: Damien Wilde
content:
![](https://9to5google.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2026/08/Moonstone-Pixelsnap-kickstand-on-Pixel-11.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600) 
Pixelsnap is one of the best things added to Pixel phones in a number of years, but it wasn’t quite a perfect first attempt. Luckily, this year those pesky magnets are a little stronger and more reliable on the Pixel 11 series.
In my testing, the magnets this year are just below the strength of the Magsafe connection on an iPhone. Things will connect more securely to the back of your phone, so you’re less likely to knock things off or encounter issues with any other accessories you might want to pair with the Pixel 11.
It’s hard to quantify without trying it out for yourself. You can sort of see in the quick demo below how there is a little extra force needed to pry the Pixelsnap kickstand from the back of the Pixel 11 over the Pixel 10. It takes less pressure from a single finger on the Pixel 10, whereas you need to actively try to remove it on the Pixel 11.
The magnets just have a little more grip, and it’s improved if the accessory you’re connecting has strong magnets already. I wouldn’t say the connection is quite as strong as when using the magnets on an iPhone, but it’s a lot closer:
We’re still sort of waiting for basically every Android OEM to jump on board with the Qi2 magnetic connection for flagships. So far, only Google, HMD (Nokia to you and me), and Motorola, with the Edge 70 Max, have bothered to add magnets to the back of devices. Most other brands, namely Samsung, have decided to rely on cases to bring the functionality. It’s a lazy implementation, but I guess it’s one that works.
That has sort of left Google to forge ahead and really make Pixelsnap work. I don’t understand why brands aren’t actively trying to implement “Magsafe” as many OEMs love copying Apple at any other time, so why avoid an easy win? My gripes aside, I’m glad that the magnets are stronger on the Pixel 11, because this means less reliance on having a case if you prefer to actually “feel” your phone day-to-day

- Pixel 11 Pro’s ‘HiLight’ is another half-baked feature burdened by bad first impressions

summary: The Pixel 11 series features stronger and more reliable Pixelsnap magnets compared to previous models. Testing shows the connection requires more force to remove accessories, bringing it closer to the strength of an iPhone's MagSafe. This improvement reduces the need for a case for users who prefer to use their phones bare.
key_points: Pixelsnap magnets on the Pixel 11 are stronger and more reliable than the previous version.
The magnetic connection is just below the strength of Apple's MagSafe.
Accessories attach more securely, reducing the likelihood of them being knocked off.
Stronger magnets allow users to comfortably use the phone without a case.

title: Google reveals first look at the future of sideloading on Android
author: Rahim Amir Noorali
content:
If you missed it, your Android freedom is due to be significantly curtailed if you've sideloaded applications in the past. Unfortunately, Google will change how you install apps outside the Play Store in less than 135 days. This means that you won’t be able to freely install open-source or third-party apps as easily as you’ve been doing so with the convenience of a few taps. And now, Google has released a sneak peek at what the future of sideloading on Android will look like.
This sneak peek comes courtesy of Mishaal Rahman, Google’s Community Engagement Manager, who announced the rollout of the first version of what Google is calling the advanced flow on the r/Android subreddit. This version is rolling out now, so you may not see it yet, but it should arrive in the coming weeks. The post also discusses Google’s future path on sideloading measures and how the system works in practice.
A brief overview of Google’s new and upcoming sideloading measures, announced back in March: all Android app developers must be registered with Google. If they aren't registered, users can install their app only through the advanced flow system. The process is a bit tiresome, as you can see from the steps outlined below:
1. Enable Developer Options on your phone if you haven’t done so already. Go to Settings > My/About Phone, tap “Build Number,” and tap it 7 times. A prompt will appear, and you’ll need to authenticate the action with your screen lock.
2. Once Developer Options have been enabled, open it and tap on “Apps from unverified developers”.
3. Next, enable “Allow apps from unverified developers”.
4. Once again, authenticate using your screen lock.
5. You’ll also need to confirm that nobody is pressuring you to change this setting.
6. Once that’s done, you’ll have to restart your phone and wait for 24 hours.
7. After 24 hours, go to the same setting and choose whether to allow apps from unverified developers for 7 days or indefinitely.
Even after enabling these settings, you’ll still see a warning when trying to install one of these apps, but you’ll be able to install them by simply tapping on “Install anyway”. This advanced flow aims to reduce scams by malicious app developers that coax many people into installing their apps.
A much more restrictive route to installs and updates
Additionally, Mishaal Rahman’s post clarifies some questions that may arise. You won’t need to keep Developer Options enabled to keep advanced flow enabled. If you mistakenly disable it, you’ll have a 10-minute window to enable it again without the hassle of a restart and a 24-hour waiting period. Advanced flow also applies to updates, so if it’s disabled after the app is installed, you won’t be able to update it without enabling advanced flow again. Installing through ADB is the only way to avoid advanced flow, so if you’re comfortable with that route, you can go for it.
The Android Developer Verifier System Service is also being rolled out and can be installed manually through the Google Play Store, hinting at an earlier appearance of the advanced flow. Meanwhile, developer verification enforcement starts September 30 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. This will first cover apps available through Google Play, HONOR App Market, OPPO App Market, Galaxy Store, Palm Store, V-Appstore, and GetApps, before covering all regions and app installations in 2027.
While these changes aren’t welcome by most of the community - at least the Reddit comments suggest they question the effectiveness of these changes, mainly asking why already-installed but unregistered apps need to have their updates blocked.
Rahman has responded quickly, explaining that some malicious apps take time to build trust with users and change their activities in future updates. He also clarified that these changes question the app's developer, not the app itself, since it doesn’t matter whether the app was downloaded from F-Droid or another app store. No matter how you look at it, Android’s future is about to change, with a mandatory and somewhat irritating flow for users trying to sideload apps.
summary: Google is rolling out a new "advanced flow" system for Android that significantly changes how users sideload applications from unverified developers. Announced by Community Engagement Manager Mishaal Rahman, the measures require unregistered developers' apps to go through a complex, multi-step installation process involving developer options, authentication, a restart, and a 24-hour waiting period. The initiative aims to reduce scams and malicious software, though enforcement and regional rollouts will begin expanding globally through 2027.
key_points: Android app developers must register with Google, or their apps will require the tiresome "advanced flow" system to install.
Installing apps from unverified developers now involves enabling Developer Options, authenticating, restarting the phone, and waiting 24 hours.
The new sideloading measures also apply to app updates, requiring advanced flow to be enabled to update unverified apps.
Developer verification enforcement begins on September 30 in select countries before expanding globally by 2027.
Installing via ADB remains the only way to bypass the new advanced flow system.

title: Intel's 28-Core bLLC Nova Lake-S Reportedly Draws 296 W PL1, Nearly 2.4X Its Expected 125 W TDP
author: Sarfraz Khan
content:
According to the latest leak, Intel's 28-core Nova Lake CPU could reach a staggering 296W PL1.
Intel's 8+16+4 bLLC Chip Rumored to be one of the Nova Lake's Highest-End Single-Tile Designs
Intel's upcoming Nova Lake-S desktop lineup appears to be one of the most aggressive ones, with power limits higher than previously expected. According to the user "Golden Pig Upgrade" (via Weibo), the Nova Lake-S CPU with a configuration of 8+16+4 will reportedly feature a PL1 (Power Limit 1) limit of 296W.
![A profile image with text in Chinese characters, alongside '28C bLLC PL1 296W' and two crying face emojis.](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Golden-Pig-Upgrade-Nova-Lake-S-296W-PL1-728x233.jpg)
This makes it potentially one of the most power-hungry mainstream desktop CPUs Intel has produced. The leaked configuration has been confirmed by previous reports, which state that the configuration will include 8 Cove P-Cores, 16 Arctic Wolf E-Cores, and 4 LP-E cores, which will result in a total of 28 CPU cores. We know from previous reports that this is going to be used for a single-compute-tile Nova Lake-S processor, which can be paired with Intel's new bLLC, or Big Last-Level Cache.
However, what makes it an interesting CPU is its 296W PL1 figure, as we have previously seen that the leaked specifications have placed this 28-core bLLC model at a 125W TDP, while the higher-end enthusiast models are expected to reach 175W. A 296W PL1 represents a substantial increase over the nominal thermal design rating, although PL1 and TDP are not interchangeable specifications.
This 8+16+4 core CPU will supposedly carry 144 MB of bLLC alongside the cache provided by the CPU cores. The Intel bLLC technology is designed to compete with AMD's 3D V-Cache technology, and from previous leaks, we know of as many as four major bLLC configurations with up to 52 cores and 288 MB of cache, according to reports from early 2026.
![](https://cdn.wccftech.com/files/placeholder-desktop.png) 
Intel Nova Lake-S Desktop CPU Die Configurations:
| Die Config | Variant | Core Config | LPE Cores | Cache | CPU PCIe Lanes | GPU Cores | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8C | Single Compute Tile | 4P+0E | 4LPE | Standard | 24 Gen5 | 2 Xe3 | 
| 16C | Single Compute Tile | 4P+8E | 4LPE | Standard | 24 Gen5 | 2 Xe3 | 
| 28C | Single Compute Tile | 8P+16E | 4LPE | Standard | 24 Gen5 | 2 Xe3 | 
| 28C | Single Compute Tile | 8P+16E | 4LPE | bLLC "Big LLC" | 24 Gen5 | 2 Xe3 | 
| 52C | Dual Compute Tile | 2x 8P+16E | 4LPE | bLLC "Big LLC" | 24 Gen5 | 2 Xe3 | 
Keep in mind that some Nova Lake S chips can reach as high as 474W when it comes to PL2, but those are much larger dual-tile processors, and with such a high PL1 limit for a single-tile CPUs, cooling can be a challenge. That said, Intel appears to be willing to trade substantially higher power consumption for performance. With such a configuration, the 28-core bLLC-equipped Nova Lake-S CPU could become one of the most powerful enthusiast-grade processor for gaming and productivity.
News Source: Weibo
